bug_semantics: An authenticated Project Manager or Owner can store a repository git_url beginning with Git's --upload-pack= option. The server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value directly after `git ls-remote` without an end-of-options delimiter; Git parses it as an option and invokes the attacker-selected upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process.
flaw_origin: Commit a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from running `git ls-remote origin <branch>` in the already-cloned repository to running `git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch>` in the temporary directory. That single-line data-flow change first placed the stored, attacker-controlled GitURL in Git's option-parsing position; the existing makeCmd helper appended the arguments to exec.Command("git") without `--`.
ai_marker: absent — `git cat-file -p a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f` shows human author and committer `Denis Gukov <fiftin@outlook.com>`, the one-line message `fix(be): bug with getting remote commit`, no trailers, no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with marker, and no bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/semaphoreui/semaphore/security/advisories/GHSA-xp7j-h7jc-4w8p documents the exact route-to-sink chain: repository GitURL is stored without option validation, GetLastRemoteCommitHash calls cmd_git `ls-remote` without `--`, and a project schedule triggers it in the server process. The assigned GHSA-93jq-5gw9-rx3q is an unreviewed alias of that issue; NVD now marks assigned CVE-2026-73682 rejected in favor of CVE-2026-73294.

`git log -L ':GetLastRemoteCommitHash:lib/GitRepository.go' 40e018aaa19cdcd33e8e8882095b19926fb1db2e^` traces the vulnerable call to a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f. Its diff replaces literal `origin` with `r.Repository.GetGitURL()` in `ls-remote`; later commit 40e018aaa19cdcd33e8e8882095b19926fb1db2e only extracts the same code into CmdGitClient, so it is a move/refactor rather than the BIC.

Direct parent-tree verification with `git show 1993a14fb6b484d4ac323700ee19cc0aaf20086f:lib/GitRepository.go` shows GetLastRemoteCommitHash calling `r.output(GitRepositoryRepoDir, "ls-remote", "origin", r.Repository.GitBranch)`. `git show a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f:lib/GitRepository.go` instead shows `GitRepositoryTmpDir` and `r.Repository.GetGitURL()`. Thus the advisory's vulnerable URL-to-ls-remote flow is absent in the immediate parent and present in the BIC.

The BIC tree's lib/GitRepository.go makeCmd uses `exec.Command("git")` followed by `cmd.Args = append(cmd.Args, args...)`; no end-of-options marker separates the newly introduced GitURL argument from Git options.

Direct release-line fix a7a7a33a64aea382a0726b3722856f298663eacf (`fix(git): validate url`) adds ValidateGitURL to reject trimmed URLs beginning with `-` and inserts `--end-of-options` before GitURL in Clone, GetLastRemoteCommitHash, and GetRemoteBranches. Its immediate parent is eb841c8d5891189b13fedbd269bbcf2d5e4e319d, the commit peeled by tag v2.18.16. The parallel develop-line commit 7e8a9434bd81b82cf42220151c74801ea97542d6 carries the identical source patch but is not the release-line direct fix.

Version membership checks (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) return success for the BIC and failure for a7a7a33a64aea382a0726b3722856f298663eacf at v2.18.12, v2.18.13, and v2.18.16; both return success at v2.18.17 and v2.18.20. Therefore the BIC predates every listed affected build and the direct fix is included by the claimed 2.18.20 patched boundary (repository history shows it actually first landed in v2.18.17).

The assigned advisory's referenced 5d87656a680600125fe78edec1f7a0d10484b52c is the v2.18.20 tip but its diff only validates template/task playbook paths and does not touch GitURL or CmdGitClient. It is not the direct fix; v2.18.20 inherits the real GitURL fix a7a7a33a64aea382a0726b3722856f298663eacf through ancestry.
`git cat-file -p a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f` establishes a single-parent, non-squash BIC with parent 1993a14fb6b484d4ac323700ee19cc0aaf20086f and contains no commit-object AI signal.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins at a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f: the schedule polling function already existed, but its parent used the configured local remote name `origin`, so attacker-controlled GitURL could not occupy an option slot on this path. The BIC deliberately changed that operand to the raw repository URL and ran from the temporary directory. Existing command construction then preserved the untrusted value as a Git argv element but omitted an end-of-options delimiter, allowing `--upload-pack=...` to be interpreted as a Git option and executed. History following both the original file and the extracted CmdGitClient function shows later edits preserved this line until the release-line fix a7a7a33a64aea382a0726b3722856f298663eacf added both input validation and argv delimiting. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent human commit, not a squash aggregate; its exact commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI trailer or bot marker. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
